root_cause.text: AppArmor's verify_dfa() applied the DEFAULT_TABLE bounds check only to non-differentially encoded DFA states, so differential-encoding traversal could use an unchecked DEFAULT_TABLE entry as a state index and access memory out of bounds.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `!(BASE_TABLE(dfa)[i] & MATCH_FLAG_DIFF_ENCODE)` from the `DEFAULT_TABLE(dfa)[i] >= state_count` check and the commit/CVE state that during differential encoding `k = DEFAULT_TABLE[j]` was used as an array index without validation, causing out-of-bounds reads and writes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix DFA verification to always reject out-of-bounds default state indices and report the error explicitly.
intent_record.what: The conditional in verify_dfa() was changed from only rejecting out-of-bounds DEFAULT_TABLE(dfa)[i] values when MATCH_FLAG_DIFF_ENCODE was not set to rejecting any DEFAULT_TABLE(dfa)[i] value that is greater than or equal to state_count, and an error log message was added before exiting in that case.
intent_record.how: At runtime, DFA verification now always validates that each default state index is within bounds regardless of encoding flags, and emits an explicit error when it is not, preventing invalid default-state references from passing verification.

candidates.rationale: This condition is the core flaw: it restricts the DEFAULT_TABLE bounds check to only non-differentially encoded states, leaving differential-encoded states unchecked and allowing out-of-bounds state indices.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional wrongly limits DEFAULT_TABLE bounds validation to only non-differentially encoded states. As a result, differentially encoded states bypass verification and can later use an unchecked default-state index, leading to out-of-bounds access.
